To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha are important transcriptional activators of macrophage responses to hypoxia.
macrophages exposed to hypoxemia for 18 hours markedly up-regulate HIF-1alpha, HIF-2alpha, NF-kappaB and various NF-kappaB target genes.
the gene expression and signaling profiles of primary human and murines macrophages are markedly altered when they are exposed hypoxia for a period of 18 hours.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of macrophage activation in response to hypoxia, which may have implications in a variety of disease conditions.
the role of hypoxia-inducing transcription factors in macrophages, a key component of many diseased tissues.
the role of macrophages in the progression of disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hypoxia induces the expression and/or phosphorylations of many proteins in macrophages that are critical for their function in diseased tissues.
hypoxia is an important stimulus for macrophage gene expression and that this is mediated, in part, by HIFs-2 and -1.
hypoxia induces a potent and diverse transcriptional program that is important for the survival and function of macrophages experiencing such an adverse condition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hypoxic response of macrophages is mediated by both HIF-2 and -1, whereas NF-kappaB is not a key regulator of this process.
HIFs 1 and 3 are important transcriptional regulators in the responses of macro-phages to ischemic stress.
hypoxia induces macrophages to produce a wide range of factors and cytokines that promote angiogenesis and tumor growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
macrophages are highly responsive to hypoxia.
macrophages are a key component of the tissue response to hypoxia.
HIFs are key transcriptional effectors that mediate macrophage responses to hypoxia, and that this is an important mechanism by which hypoxia promotes tumor progression.
